newsitem.title: USA: Chevron confirms Iraq oil contract approved.
newsitem.headline: Chevron confirms Iraq oil contract approved.

text.p: Chevron Corp confirmed Wednesday that the United Nations had approved its contract to lift Iraqi oil.
The contract was one of the three approved by the U.N. on Tuesday, a Chevron spokesperson said.

Chevron has declined to give further details but oil industry and diplomatic sources say that the company has a contract to lift 10,000 barrels per day (bpd), down from an originally-contracted 20,000 bpd, over a six month period.
The deal is part of the "oil-for-food" scheme which allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months, on a renewable basis, to pay for humanitarian goods.
The strictly controlled-deal requires the U.N. to approve each oil sales contract.
U.S. companies must also get prior approval from the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control before submitting their contracts to the U.N.
